title: Generic Problem and a hedged Appetite — both pressed, flagged, disclosed, approved anyway
notes: **Why there is no `cappedAttempts` here, and what stands in for it.** #59's
outcome for 02a is that Problem and Appetite are each pressed to the cap —
base question plus two follow-ups, three asks — and then accepted with a
flag. That number is currently unassertable, and both reasons are structural
and live in the shared checker. Verified against the hand-built positive
control, where a fully correct run fails both cap checks:
1. Appetite's base question legitimately matches every one of its asks.
SKILL.md's own re-ask is "Appetite is fixed before we shape the
solution — which tier are you committing to?" and it tells the skill to
"offer exactly those two tiers" every time, so the escalation is the
same question again. `attemptsOn` reads the repeat as an ambiguous
pattern and refuses to produce a number — on the one field whose whole
point in this scenario is that it gets re-asked.
2. The Problem window is closed by a scan that looks past its own end.
`fieldWindow` marks a later field ambiguous when that field's pattern
matches twice *anywhere after* the window opens, not — as this suite's
README says — inside the span being measured. So the skill asking for a
second Riskiest Assumption candidate at turn 9, which SKILL.md provides
for and the recorded 01 run does, makes turn 0's Problem window
ambiguous and fails a cap check eight turns earlier.
Declaring the key anyway would be a guaranteed false fail of the whole
scenario, and this is where the suite says to put an outcome nothing grades.
What is asserted instead is the lower bound, which is the half that catches a
real misbehaviour: `problemPressedOnSwapTest` and `appetitePressedForTier`
fail a skill that accepts a category as a Problem or a calendar estimate as
an Appetite. Nothing here catches a skill that presses *four* times;
`maxAgentTurns` is the only ceiling and it is a crude aggregate one.
**`sketchAndAssumptionsClean` is a stand-in too.** #59 says the Solution
sketch and the assumption come out clean. The shared `disclosedFlags` set —
which is what `judge.mjs` reads to excuse a failing criterion — is computed
by a paragraph-head heuristic that registers both of those fields as flagged
from nothing but the `##` headings of the draft the skill pastes into chat,
and from the gate-check sentence that says they are clean. On the positive
control it reports `Solution sketch` as disclosed against a run that flagged
nothing of the sort. The two assertions here are narrower and pattern-based;
the real fix is `disclosedFlags` set-equal to `flaggedFields`, in the
checker.
**Where the evidence for both claims is.** That a fully correct run fails
both cap checks, and that `disclosedFlags` reports the Solution sketch as
disclosed against a run that flagged nothing of the sort, were established
against positive-controls/pressed-flagged-disclosed-approved.json. That file
used to be graded by hand; `node evals/harness/controls.mjs $E` now runs it
beside every other control, and it passes 31 of 31 as this scenario is
currently written.
